name: genesis-vision
content:
.TH GENESIS-VISION 7 "November 2026" "Genesis 0.2.0" "Genesis Manual"
.SH NAME
genesis-vision \- the visual perception and optic faculties of Genesis
.SH SYNOPSIS
.nf
\fBAndroid Camera2\fR -> RGB24 -> daemon optic capture -> optic mapping
\fBLinux V4L2\fR -> daemon optic capture -> optic mapping
\fBgenesis_client.optic_nerve.latest_frame()\fR -> mind-side perception
.fi
.SH DESCRIPTION
Genesis has one visual-afferent frame contract and one mind-side
perception pathway. Platform adapters acquire camera frames; the
daemon validates and publishes them; the Python mind reads the
canonical optic mapping and processes the image through its
occipital faculties. The Android adapter is a hardware boundary,
not a second perception system.
.SS Android Camera2
The Android companion application runs as a foreground camera
service because Android and Termux have separate application
identities and permission boundaries. It defaults to the
front-facing camera; the activity can select the front or rear
camera. If the requested lens is unavailable, the service reports
an error rather than silently substituting another camera.
.PP
The adapter requests a YUV_420_888 output size no larger than
640x480, converts the planes to packed RGB24, and targets up to
10 frames per second. Its preview capture request uses
.B CONTROL_MODE_AUTO
and a preview template. The adapter selects an available
auto-exposure target frame-rate range when one fits its low-rate
capture policy. The adapter does not explicitly override sensor exposure
time, ISO, exposure compensation, autofocus mode or regions, or
white-balance mode. Those behaviors are left to the Camera2
preview-template defaults and the device implementation; Genesis
does not expose manual physical-camera controls as configurable
settings here.
.PP
The Android service hosts a loopback TCP listener at
.IR 127.0.0.1:8765 .
The daemon connects outward. Each frame packet contains the
.IR GOPT
magic, width, height, payload length (32-bit big-endian integers),
and packed RGB24 pixels. The daemon checks dimensions and payload
length before publishing the frame.
.SS Linux V4L2
On Linux, the daemon's capture limb opens the device selected by
.B GENESIS_CAMERA
(default
.IR /dev/video0 ),
requests 640x480 RGB24, and falls back to YUYV if RGB24 is not
available. This capture limb is part of the daemon; there is no
separate current
.B genesis-retina
executable.
.SS Canonical optic mapping
The daemon publishes both platform paths through
.IR /genesis_optic_nerve .
The mapping uses a 28-byte header, a frame payload, and a seqlock
sequence counter so readers can reject a frame being written.
Linux uses POSIX shared memory; Android uses a file-backed mapping.
The Python reader is
.IR genesis_client/optic_nerve.py ;
.B latest_frame()
returns the most recent available image to the existing mind-side
pipeline. Android TCP is only the boundary between the Android
camera sandbox and Termux; it is not a Python receiver or alternate
perception path.
.SS Ocular body model
The daemon also exposes ocular state to the mind:
.IP \\(bu 2
.B Pupil
diameter is modeled from 2 to 8 mm. Its area determines the
retinal-irradiance gain relative to a 4.5 mm reference pupil:
.RI ( d / 4.5 )^2 .
The modeled gain affects the photoreceptor input; it does not
change the phone camera's physical exposure.
.IP \\(bu 2
.B Accommodation
is requested by the mind through
.B SET_FOCUS
in metres and converted to a bounded ciliary drive. The software
optics layer applies a global depth-of-field blur based on pupil
and focus distance. It has no depth map or per-object focal plane,
so it cannot produce spatially selective bokeh or physically
refocus the phone lens.
.IP \\(bu 2
.B Eyelid
transmission attenuates the image according to the modeled lid
state. The voluntary component is set through
.BR SET_LID .
.IP \\(bu 2
.B Thalamic relay gain
is adjusted through
.B SET_OPTIC_GAIN
within bounded limits and cannot reopen a gate closed by sleep
state.
.SS Retinal and cortical processing
The mind-side pathway in
.I python/occipital_lobe/perception/
processes the captured frame in stages:
.IP \\(bu 2
.B Optics
applies the modeled mirror view when requested, eyelid
attenuation, and pupil/focus-dependent blur.
.IP \\(bu 2
.B Illumination
uses a Retinex-style luminance decomposition to estimate
illuminant, reflectance, light direction, and shadows. A partial
von Kries chromatic adaptation is applied to the RGB image
(adaptation strength 0.8; per-channel gains clamped to 0.5--2.0).
This corrects estimated color cast; it does not increase sensor
exposure or reconstruct detail lost in darkness, clipping, or blur.
.IP \\(bu 2
.B Phototransduction
runs a stateful mathematical cone-response cascade, including
visual-pigment and PDE activation, cGMP, calcium feedback, and
photocurrent. The brightness input is derived from the processed
image and modeled pupil irradiance.
.IP \\(bu 2
.B Cortical perception
extracts color and regional color, objects, faces, V1 sparse
features, and two-view motion/parallax information. Structured
scene data is integrated with salience, memory, and other cognitive
pathways; the pipeline does not reduce the full image to the
daemon's scalar channels.
.SS Brightness and image quality
The scene reports a brightness measure derived from the HSV value
channel. This is a measurement, not a camera brightness control.
The Android adapter does not add a software brightness, contrast,
or sharpening filter before transmission. Illumination adaptation
changes estimated chromatic balance, not the camera's exposure.
.PP
A low brightness value can reflect a dark scene, underexposure,
or both. Pupil dilation in the software model cannot create photons
or recover details the sensor did not capture. Focus blur, motion
blur, small faces, occlusion, and low resolution can also reduce
recognition performance.
.SS Face detection and identity
Face recognition is an optional mind-side faculty implemented in
.I python/occipital_lobe/perception/recognition.py
using OpenCV YuNet for detection and SFace for 128-dimensional
face embeddings. Detection and identity matching are separate:
detecting a face does not establish who the person is.
.PP
The current source parameters are:
.IP \\(bu 2
YuNet score threshold 0.6, non-maximum suppression threshold 0.3,
and top-k limit 5000.
.IP \\(bu 2
Named identity cosine-similarity threshold 0.4. A higher threshold
is stricter and can increase false negatives; lowering it can
increase false matches.
.IP \\(bu 2
Anonymous-cluster cosine-similarity threshold 0.45. A recurring
unidentified face can receive a stable
.I face:N
key without a name.
.IP \\(bu 2
At most 20 embeddings are retained per named identity and per
anonymous cluster; at most 64 anonymous clusters are retained.
A cluster is persisted only after at least two sightings.
.PP
.B /register-face
registers the largest detected face in the current frame under the
provided name. If no face is detected or the recognition models
are unavailable, registration fails. The
.B /faces
command reports known identities and recent sightings. These
thresholds are implementation parameters, not camera brightness
settings or universal guarantees of identity.
.PP
Named embeddings are stored in
.I $DATA_DIR/known_faces.json ;
anonymous clusters are stored in
.IR $DATA_DIR/face_clusters.json .
The YuNet and SFace ONNX files must be present in
.IR $DATA_DIR/models/ .
Model availability proves only that the models can be loaded; it
does not prove successful recognition on a particular live camera,
face, or lighting condition.
.SS Commands and diagnostics
.TP
.B /look
Ask Genesis to process the latest available optic frame.
.TP
.B /look screen
Ask Genesis to process the screen-capture nerve, when available.
.TP
.BR /register-face " \\fIname\\fR"
Register the largest face detected in the current frame.
.TP
.B /faces
Inspect known identities and recent anonymous or named sightings.
.PP
On Android, launch the Genesis Camera Adapter activity and inspect
its foreground notification for camera selection, permission,
capture-session, daemon-connection, and first-frame status. Device
logs can be inspected with the
.B logcat
command using the
.I GenesisCamera
tag (filter the Android log by that tag). On Linux, inspect the daemon log for V4L2 open, format
negotiation, and frame-publication messages.
.SH FILES
.TP
.I /genesis_optic_nerve
Canonical frame mapping (POSIX shared memory on Linux; file-backed
mapping on Android).
.TP
.I $DATA_DIR/known_faces.json
Persisted named face embeddings.
.TP
.I $DATA_DIR/face_clusters.json
Persisted anonymous face clusters.
.TP
.I $DATA_DIR/daemon.log
Daemon capture and optic-nerve diagnostics.
.TP
.I android-camera-bridge/
Android Camera2 adapter source and build configuration.
.TP
.I python/occipital_lobe/perception/
Mind-side optical, illumination, phototransduction, and recognition
faculties.
.SH LIMITATIONS
The physical capture controls are platform- and device-dependent.
Genesis currently does not expose manual Android sensor exposure,
ISO, exposure compensation, autofocus regions, or white-balance
settings through the adapter. Software pupil, accommodation,
illumination, and phototransduction models are internal perception
stages; they do not replace missing physical camera controls or
restore information absent from the captured frame.
.PP
Successful source-level integration or model loading is not
physical-device validation. Confirm live frame delivery and actual
recognition on the target device.
.SH SEE ALSO
.BR genesis (1),
.BR genesis-cli (1),
.BR genesis-daemon (8),
.BR genesis-retina (1),
.BR genesis-math (7),
.BR genesis-reasoning (7)
